mission: Descent through Levels 1 and 2 — Operations and Archive — the fortress tells its story through environment. Monitoring systems, dead comms, archive media from an era the modern Order has forgotten.
why_now: Sequential exploration — each level reveals more of the fortress's purpose
conflict: The archive is partially organized, partially chaotic — stored under time pressure. Ben can read fragments but lacks the conceptual vocabulary to understand what he's reading. Force-locks block deeper access.
turning_point: A monitoring display still functions — showing a network of nodes across the Outer Rim, most reading dead, three reading active, one reading BREACH. The network is a containment system.
opening_hook: Level 1 is a command post. The communications equipment died centuries ago but the monitoring stations retain residual power — and they're tracking something.
closing_hook: The stairwell to Level 3 descends into blue-tinged emergency lighting. The Force down there is different — not wrong but alive, pulsing with three distinct rhythms. People. Living people, sealed below.
emotional_trajectory: Archaeological wonder -> growing dread -> shock at the living Force signatures

stakes.personal: Ben is descending into something he doesn't understand
stakes.interpersonal: Desh catalogues exits and escape routes — his instincts say this is wrong
stakes.external: The monitoring system reveals a network in cascading failure

setting: Fortress interior — Level 1 (Operations) through Level 2 (Archive), descending corridor to Level 3
sensory_details: Residual power humming in walls; dust on surfaces undisturbed for centuries; archive media — holocrons, data tablets, vacuum-sealed documents; the transition from dead air above to something charged below
canon_elements_needed: Jedi holocron and archive storage technology
Living Force signatures detection and differentiation
notes: Gavran's archive voice should be felt through what he chose to keep and how he organized it — meticulous where time allowed, frantic where it didn't. The monitoring display is the bridge to Level 3.
